passage:
"Didi, can I tell you something?" Damini said on the terrace.
"Of course," said Lalremsiami.
"Sir kept my drawing and gave me zero, and I did not even copy it. He said the decision is final."
"That sounds awful."
"I felt so helpless. He is the teacher, so I just stood there."
"You do not have to swallow that or get back at him. What if you ask him politely to look at it again?"
"He might say no."
"He might. But you will have said it."
"Will you come with me?"
"I will wait outside the staff room."
Damini breathed out slowly.

qa.q: What did Sir give Damini for the drawing?
qa.a: He kept Damini's drawing and gave it zero.

qa.q: What was Damini feeling when saying "I just stood there"?
qa.a: Damini felt helpless because the teacher decided and Damini could not argue back.

qa.q: What could Damini do next to be heard without revenge?
qa.a: Damini can politely ask the teacher to look at the drawing again, with Lalremsiami waiting nearby for support.

qa.q: How might the teacher see Damini's polite request?
qa.a: The teacher may see a student who respects him but wants a fair look, and might reconsider, though he may also say no.

grounding: A child who cannot argue with an adult's decision names that helplessness to someone safe and plans to ask politely to be heard.
